bull_bear.body: 100% capex funded by internal accruals; no debt used; prioritizing capacity expansion over buybacks/dividends; sustainability investments (solar, recycling) embedded in capex
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical raw material disruption (mitigated by JG’s supplier dominance); ceramic market adoption speed; zinc price volatility (absorbed via FIFO inventory); execution delay in Dahej Phase 1
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly bullish; confident in demand sustainability; frames crises as competitive differentiators; emphasizes customer intimacy, scale, and ESG alignment; tone on recycled rubber project is 'gung-ho'
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: JG’s IATF/WHO certifications are de facto barriers to entry — no global competitor matches this; Dahej’s proximity to ceramic hub (Morbi) is a strategic play to capture unpenetrated $1B+ market; recycled rubber project could become a $500cr+ revenue stream by FY30; inventory gains are retained, not passed on — a hidden margin accelerator
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The Rs. 100 Cr Dahej project is stated to be 100% funded through internal accruals.
- Essentially debt-free balance sheet: non-current borrowings fell from INR 36 Mn (FY24) to nil in FY25 and FY26; current borrowings were INR 102 Mn (FY24), INR 1 Mn (FY25) and INR 64 Mn (FY26), against total liabilities of just INR 282 Mn in FY26.
- Balance sheet carries substantial liquidity: FY26 current investments INR 1,219 Mn (up from INR 390 Mn in FY25), cash and cash equivalents INR 162 Mn and other bank balances INR 222 Mn.
- Working capital is acknowledged as structurally heavy — 'High Working Capital' is listed among Key Strengths as a barrier; FY26 inventories were INR 918 Mn and trade receivables INR 1,710 Mn.
- Equity grew from INR 4,055 Mn (FY24) to INR 4,746 Mn (FY25) to INR 5,411 Mn (FY26); the deck discloses no dividend or buyback policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- scale: largest zinc oxide maker in India and Asia and among the top five worldwide — evidence: three plants with a combined capacity of 77,000 MTPA (including ingot), grown from a single 600 MTPA plant in 1975
- customer lock-in: long-standing qualified supplier to global tyre majors — evidence: customers include 9 of the world's 10 largest tyre manufacturers and every major Indian one; 200+ domestic and 50+ international accounts, most buying year after year; customers accepted pricing revisions when costs rose in March — against it: approximately 85% of revenue comes from the rubber and tyre sector
- licence/regulatory: pharma-grade accreditation stack that gates entry to the highest-margin end markets — evidence: Naidupeta is stated to be the only zinc oxide facility globally holding IATF certification together with WHO GMP and global pharmacopoeia (IP/USP/BP/EP) approvals
- cost position: recycling-based feedstock — evidence: the company makes zinc oxide from zinc scrap and dross, and states that the spread between low-cost scrap inputs and higher-value finished output is the single largest contributor to its profitability; raw-material and finished-product pricing are both linked to LME zinc benchmarks (pass-through)
- technology: application-specific grade portfolio — evidence: more than 90 specialised zinc oxide grades, up from over 80 a year earlier, each made to individual customer technical and regulatory specifications
- integration: by-product value chain from galvanising residue — evidence: zinc dross and zinc ash are recovered as secondary feedstock and turned into both zinc oxide and zinc sulphate (zinc sulphate produced from the company's own recycling stream)
- distribution: production close to western India's tyre, ceramics, pharma and agrochemical clusters and Gujarat ports [planned] — evidence: Dahej plant under construction on 11.43 acres, Phase 1 commissioning targeted Q3 FY27 — against it: higher freight costs and longer delivery windows have kept volumes into western plants minimal so far
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Input and raw-material cost pressure — The company says input cost pressures weighed on the first two quarters of FY26, which were sluggish before a second-half recovery.
- Macro demand softness — The company names macro softness as a reason for the sluggish first half of FY26, so volumes depend on the industrial demand cycle.
- Dependence on purchased grid electricity — The company buys grid electricity (the source of its Scope 2 emissions) and furnace combustion drives its Scope 1 emissions. It says its move to solar and other renewables is meant to reduce this dependence, so energy cost and supply remain an exposure until then.

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Incorporated in 1975 starting with a ~600 MTPA plant in Kolkata, JGCL is described as the largest manufacturer of Zinc Oxide in India with ~31% market share (as on March 30, 2025), amongst the top 5 manufacturers globally and the largest in Asia (deck footnote: 'Excluding China').
- Described as the largest zinc recycling company, with strong R&D and in-house developed recycling technology for various forms of zinc waste/scrap; it serves 200+ domestic customers and 50+ global customers in more than 10 countries with 90%+ repeat customers.
- Tyre-customer reach is stated two ways in the deck: one slide says '9/10 Global tyre manufacturers served' and 'Top 15 Indian tyre manufacturers served', while the Key Strengths slide says '9 out of Top 10 global and Top 11 domestic Tyre manufacturers are our customers'.
- High entry barriers claimed on three fronts: large tyre accounts take on average 4-5 years minimum to approve a new vendor; a global zinc-scrap sourcing network takes decades of relationships to build; and licences (IATF, WHO GMP, US/British/European Pharma, Indian Pharmacopeia) require stringent systems and capex.
- 'No China Threat' — the deck argues zinc oxide prices are determined by zinc prices on the LME, so China has no competitive edge exporting to India. Over 95% of sales are direct to end customers.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Tyre industry capex] Per recent ATMA reports cited in the deck, an estimated capex of about INR 25,000 crore has been announced by Indian tyre majors, with approx. 25% of tyres produced in India now exported.
- [Auto demand] Per ATMA, Q1 FY27 saw volume growth across major vehicle categories: PV +26.6% YoY, 2W +16.58% YoY, CV +16.48% YoY, 3W +11.32% YoY.
- [Shareholding] As on 30th June 2026: Promoters 70.99%, Public 22.79%, FII 3.21%, AIF 2.11%, DII 0.89%; marquee shareholders listed are Massachusetts Institute of Technology 2.62%, Carnelian Structural Shift Fund 1.69%, CTL Trusteeship Limited 1.24% and SBI General Insurance Company Limited 0.89%.
- [Future strategy] Stated growth strategies are: expand product portfolio, deeper penetration in domestic markets, diversify customer applications in end-user industries, ramp-up of the zinc sulphate business, and expansion to new geographies.
- [Geography] Geographical presence listed as India, Australia, other SAARC countries, Thailand and Europe, with a slide annotation reading 'Constitutes 99.25% of total exports from India' whose subject is ambiguous in the extract.

business.body: J.G. Chemicals makes zinc oxide from recycled zinc scrap and dross (galvanising by-products) using the dry, high-temperature French Process, and supplies application-specific grades to more than 20 industries, led by tyres and rubber, ceramics, pharmaceuticals, agriculture and speciality chemicals. It also makes zinc sulphate from its own recycling stream for agricultural micronutrient use. Customers include 9 of the world's 10 largest tyre makers and every major Indian tyre maker, and it exports under the LUXMI brand.

latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: double-digit volume growth expected in FY27; margin: 10-11% baseline, targeting 13-14% with higher-value products; order inflow: strong visibility from tire capex (INR20,000cr over 3 yrs); capex/commissioning: Dahej Phase 1 commissioning H1FY27, brownfield debottlenecking at Naidupeta by Dec26, total capex INR100cr from internal accruals
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Recycled rubber intermediates (pilot validated, commercial project in pipeline); ceramic market entry via Dahej (near Morbi hub); non-rubber share expansion (targeting 30%+ of revenue); potential eastern capacity expansion
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Four parallel growth priorities: capacity, geography, market mix and margin.
- Capacity ahead of demand: expand while existing plants run at close to 80% of achievable capacity, through a greenfield plant at Dahej, Gujarat and debottlenecking at Naidupeta, Andhra Pradesh.
- Geography: use the Dahej plant to serve western India's tyre, ceramics, pharmaceutical and agrochemical clusters (including Morbi, India's largest ceramics cluster) locally and gain access to export shipping lanes through Gujarat ports.
- Market-mix diversification away from tyres: ceramics and speciality chemicals as the most immediate opportunity, pharmaceuticals and cosmetics as the highest-margin segment, zinc sulphate for agriculture, and an early presence in batteries and electronics.
- Margin through product mix: grow the share of premium specialised zinc oxide grades (over 90 now, up from over 80 a year earlier).
- Wallet-share expansion with tyre customers through a recycled-rubber offering under customer evaluation.
- Self-funded growth: expansion financed entirely from internal accruals with no recourse to debt.
- Deepen recycling across processes and reduce reliance on virgin materials as the business grows.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Expansion runs on two tracks. At Dahej, Gujarat, a new plant is under construction on 11.43 acres in a chemical investment zone at a stated cost of ₹1000 mn, funded entirely from internal accruals; the Board approved the Dahej capex in August 2025 (land procurement for future expansion was approved in May 2025). Civil construction and equipment installation are in progress and Phase 1 commissioning is targeted for Q3 FY27; management puts break-even at 30–35% utilisation. At Naidupeta, Andhra Pradesh, a debottlenecking initiative is raising output from the existing assets and is expected to finish by December 2026. Together these are to lift installed capacity of zinc products from around 77,000 MTPA to over 122,000 MTPA by FY29, while existing plants run at close to 80% of achievable capacity. Dahej places manufacturing near western India's tyre, ceramics (Morbi), pharmaceutical and agrochemical clusters and near the Gujarat ports for exports.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Volume growth was double-digit for FY26 and stepped up in the closing quarter, after a sluggish first half.
- Product mix is expected to be the key margin lever as premium grades form a growing share of sales, replacing volume as the historical growth driver.
- Feedstock economics: the spread between low-cost scrap inputs and higher-value finished output is the single largest contributor to profitability.
- Management expects EBITDA margins to rise with premiumisation, diversification, higher efficiency and operating leverage.
- Local production at Dahej is expected to turn existing western India relationships into active accounts, previously limited by higher freight costs and longer delivery windows.
- Cleaner, more responsible supply chains are becoming a requirement across global industry, which management expects to make its recycling-led capability more valuable.
- Customers accepted pricing revisions when energy and input costs rose sharply in March.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: JG Chemicals delivered record FY26 financials driven by robust tire demand and GST-led auto revival, with Dahej capacity expansion and recycled rubber R&D creating multi-year growth visibility; margin resilience despite March raw material spikes confirms pricing power and supply chain dominance, positioning JG as the indispensable zinc solutions partner for global tire and emerging ceramic markets.

summary.oneLiner: India's largest zinc oxide manufacturer and a recycling-based producer that turns zinc scrap and dross into more than 90 specialised grades, mainly for the tyre and rubber industry.
summary.business: J.G. Chemicals makes zinc oxide from recycled zinc scrap and dross (galvanising by-products) using the dry, high-temperature French Process, and supplies application-specific grades to more than 20 industries, led by tyres and rubber, ceramics, pharmaceuticals, agriculture and speciality chemicals. It also makes zinc sulphate from its own recycling stream for agricultural micronutrient use. Customers include 9 of the world's 10 largest tyre makers and every major Indian tyre maker, and it exports under the LUXMI brand.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Volume growth was double-digit for FY26 and stepped up in the closing quarter, after a sluggish first half.
- Product mix is expected to be the key margin lever as premium grades form a growing share of sales, replacing volume as the historical growth driver.
- Feedstock economics: the spread between low-cost scrap inputs and higher-value finished output is the single largest contributor to profitability.
- Management expects EBITDA margins to rise with premiumisation, diversification, higher efficiency and operating leverage.
- Local production at Dahej is expected to turn existing western India relationships into active accounts, previously limited by higher freight costs and longer delivery windows.
- Cleaner, more responsible supply chains are becoming a requirement across global industry, which management expects to make its recycling-led capability more valuable.
- Customers accepted pricing revisions when energy and input costs rose sharply in March.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin 9.4% in Q4 suppressed by March energy cost spike (doubled) and spot zinc dross procurement (LME surge); pricing fully passed on from April 1, 2026; inventory gains from Q3-Q1 zinc price rise partially offset by March cost shock; baseline margin 10-11%, target 13-14% with premium grades

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: 100% capex funded by internal accruals; no debt used; prioritizing capacity expansion over buybacks/dividends; sustainability investments (solar, recycling) embedded in capex

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Expansion runs on two tracks. At Dahej, Gujarat, a new plant is under construction on 11.43 acres in a chemical investment zone at a stated cost of ₹1000 mn, funded entirely from internal accruals; the Board approved the Dahej capex in August 2025 (land procurement for future expansion was approved in May 2025). Civil construction and equipment installation are in progress and Phase 1 commissioning is targeted for Q3 FY27; management puts break-even at 30–35% utilisation. At Naidupeta, Andhra Pradesh, a debottlenecking initiative is raising output from the existing assets and is expected to finish by December 2026. Together these are to lift installed capacity of zinc products from around 77,000 MTPA to over 122,000 MTPA by FY29, while existing plants run at close to 80% of achievable capacity. Dahej places manufacturing near western India's tyre, ceramics (Morbi), pharmaceutical and agrochemical clusters and near the Gujarat ports for exports.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- scale: largest zinc oxide maker in India and Asia and among the top five worldwide — evidence: three plants with a combined capacity of 77,000 MTPA (including ingot), grown from a single 600 MTPA plant in 1975
- customer lock-in: long-standing qualified supplier to global tyre majors — evidence: customers include 9 of the world's 10 largest tyre manufacturers and every major Indian one; 200+ domestic and 50+ international accounts, most buying year after year; customers accepted pricing revisions when costs rose in March — against it: approximately 85% of revenue comes from the rubber and tyre sector
- licence/regulatory: pharma-grade accreditation stack that gates entry to the highest-margin end markets — evidence: Naidupeta is stated to be the only zinc oxide facility globally holding IATF certification together with WHO GMP and global pharmacopoeia (IP/USP/BP/EP) approvals
- cost position: recycling-based feedstock — evidence: the company makes zinc oxide from zinc scrap and dross, and states that the spread between low-cost scrap inputs and higher-value finished output is the single largest contributor to its profitability; raw-material and finished-product pricing are both linked to LME zinc benchmarks (pass-through)
- technology: application-specific grade portfolio — evidence: more than 90 specialised zinc oxide grades, up from over 80 a year earlier, each made to individual customer technical and regulatory specifications
- integration: by-product value chain from galvanising residue — evidence: zinc dross and zinc ash are recovered as secondary feedstock and turned into both zinc oxide and zinc sulphate (zinc sulphate produced from the company's own recycling stream)
- distribution: production close to western India's tyre, ceramics, pharma and agrochemical clusters and Gujarat ports [planned] — evidence: Dahej plant under construction on 11.43 acres, Phase 1 commissioning targeted Q3 FY27 — against it: higher freight costs and longer delivery windows have kept volumes into western plants minimal so far

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Geopolitical raw material disruption (mitigated by JG’s supplier dominance); ceramic market adoption speed; zinc price volatility (absorbed via FIFO inventory); execution delay in Dahej Phase 1

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: JG’s IATF/WHO certifications are de facto barriers to entry — no global competitor matches this; Dahej’s proximity to ceramic hub (Morbi) is a strategic play to capture unpenetrated $1B+ market; recycled rubber project could become a $500cr+ revenue stream by FY30; inventory gains are retained, not passed on — a hidden margin accelerator

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Four parallel growth priorities: capacity, geography, market mix and margin.
- Capacity ahead of demand: expand while existing plants run at close to 80% of achievable capacity, through a greenfield plant at Dahej, Gujarat and debottlenecking at Naidupeta, Andhra Pradesh.
- Geography: use the Dahej plant to serve western India's tyre, ceramics, pharmaceutical and agrochemical clusters (including Morbi, India's largest ceramics cluster) locally and gain access to export shipping lanes through Gujarat ports.
- Market-mix diversification away from tyres: ceramics and speciality chemicals as the most …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Tyre industry capex] Per recent ATMA reports cited in the deck, an estimated capex of about INR 25,000 crore has been announced by Indian tyre majors, with approx. 25% of tyres produced in India now exported.
- [Auto demand] Per ATMA, Q1 FY27 saw volume growth across major vehicle categories: PV +26.6% YoY, 2W +16.58% YoY, CV +16.48% YoY, 3W +11.32% YoY.
- [Shareholding] As on 30th June 2026: Promoters 70.99%, Public 22.79%, FII 3.21%, AIF 2.11%, DII 0.89%; marquee shareholders listed are Massachusetts Institute of Technology 2.62%, Carnelian Structural Shift Fund 1.69%, CTL Trusteeship Limited 1.24% and SBI General Insurance Company Limited 0.89%.
- [Future strategy] Stated growth strategies are: expand product portfolio, deeper penetration in domestic markets, diversify customer applications in end-user industries, ramp-up of the zinc sulphate business, and expansion to new geographies.
- [Geography] Geographical presence listed as India, Australia, other SAARC countries, Thailand and Europe, with a slide annotation reading 'Constitutes 99.25% of total exports from India' whose subject is ambiguous in the extract.

themes.title: Import-substitution / China+1 specialty chemicals
themes.need: After the worst agrochem/chemicals year in living memory, the cycle is turning on China+1 reshoring and global pigment/dye consolidation. SUDARSCHEM is now #2 global pigment player post-Heubach; SUMICHEM posted record FY26 margins; AETHER/ANURAS/DEEPAKNTR/CLEAN add CRAMS + backward-integration; war-driven RM/freight inflation is being passed through. Q1FY27 shows the reshoring build-out actually landing: HSCL grew consolidated revenue 28% to INR 1,432cr with PAT INR 228cr (+27%) at a 22% EBITDA margin while opening three new value ladders in a single quarter (carbon nanotube 200 MTPA by Q4FY27, super-speciality carbon black 6,000 MTPA by FY28, and India's first commercial anthraquinone/carbazole plant), all self-funded with no incremental debt; TATVA grew revenue 43% YoY and delivered its first commercial-plant-scale semiconductor batch, qualified by the customer and called 'the glaring achievement of the past decade' (though commercialisation is explicitly not before Q4 CY2028); FCL tripled total income to INR 386.72cr (+165%) with Texas capacity nearly doubled to 148,000 MTPA and already running 63% on a single shift, so its next revenue leg needs only USD 1-2mn of capex.
themes.driver: Volume rebound as destocking ends; price hikes sticking; new value-ladder commissioning (HSCL CNT/carbon black) and semiconductor-materials qualification (TATVA).
